Ask for an app PIN (and optionally your fingerprint) when opening AdCtrl. While locked, your server passwords stay encrypted with the PIN and nothing is sent to your servers, unless you turned on background checks

AdCtrl has no analytics or tracking. It only talks to your own AdGuard Home servers. While AdCtrl is locked, the Quick Settings tile only opens the app, so nobody can pause protection without your PIN, and the widget only says that AdCtrl is locked.

Background checks are on, so they can still sign in while AdCtrl is locked: your server passwords are then only encrypted with the Android Keystore, as without the app lock, and the widget keeps showing your server. Turn off background checks in Notifications to keep them sealed with your PIN too. The Quick Settings tile still only opens the app while AdCtrl is locked. AdCtrl has no analytics or tracking.

Background checks and what to notify about
Notifications are blocked: tap to allow them

AdGuard Home can\'t send notifications itself, so AdCtrl checks your servers in the background and tells you when protection is off or paused for too long, a server can\'t be reached, filter lists stop updating or a new version is out. The checks only read; nothing changes on your servers.
Notifications are blocked for AdCtrl, so the background checks can\'t tell you anything.
Looks at every saved server and notifies about new problems

Android runs background checks at most every 15 minutes, and can delay them to save battery. They only talk to your own AdGuard Home servers. With the app lock on, your server passwords stay usable in the background while these checks are on (see Privacy and security).
